title: The Giveaway You Entered
intro: A message says you won a giveaway. This time you really did enter one last week.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

banner.text: Reply to your comment on their giveaway post

screen.context: Last week you commented on Meridu Store's public giveaway post. Their real account is @meridu_store.

msg.text: Congratulations! You won the desk lamp from our public giveaway.
We have also announced the winners in a post on our page.
Prizes are free to receive. We only need a delivery address, which you can send through our website's contact form.
We will never ask for payment, a card or a code.

reply.label: A reply to your own comment
reply.lens: It answers the giveaway you entered, not a random DM.
reply.why: It matches something you did. That is a strong honest sign.

name.label: Shop name
name.why: A name alone proves nothing, so check the handle and the page.

handle.label: The shop's real account
handle.lens: @meridu_store is the real account, six years old.
handle.why: It matches the real handle on the shop's own website.

won.label: You did enter
won.lens: You commented on that giveaway post last week.
won.why: A prize for a contest you entered is normal.

public.label: Announced publicly too
public.lens: The winners are also posted on the page.
public.why: Real giveaways announce winners in public.

free.label: Prize is free
free.lens: It asks only for a delivery address, through the shop's own site.
free.why: Real prizes are free and use the shop's own website.

nopay.label: Never asks for payment
nopay.lens: It says it will never ask for payment, card or code.
nopay.why: Honest senders say this up front.

logo.label: Shop logo
logo.why: Logos are easy to copy, so they prove little alone.

actions.label: Check the shop's page, then send my address through its website form

go_ahead.line: The winner post was on the shop's page. You sent your address through the real site, and the lamp arrived free on Thursday.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real message, and you stayed careful.

block_report.line: That was a real message. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: You entered, the account is the real one, winners were announced in public, and nothing was asked of you but an address through the shop's own site.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A prize for a contest you really entered, from the real account, with no payment, is honest. Check the shop's own page first.

quick_check.q: What made this giveaway message honest?

options.text: You had entered, it came from the real account, winners were public and nothing was asked but an address through the shop's own site

quick_check.explain: You entered, it is the real account, nothing to pay: these three together.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Real account on the shop's site?
